journal.title: Wed Sep 30 review: +$7.5 on the day; Micron beat and raise held; Thursday: one ruling trade at most
journal.body:

What worked:
- Staying out. QTTB faded from +16% pre-market to -2.8% (J0019). The Sep 29 scan names mostly fell: JELD -7.5%, WW -9.6%, CCL -2.3%, SDEV -20.8%, SVRN -25.8% (movers --follow-up), which is consistent with the jump study.
- Holding MUU through the report. Micron beat revenue by 5.3% and EPS by 5.0% and guided 6% above consensus (J0022). After hours MU is +0.6-0.8% and MUU 7.30-37.51.
What didn't:
- Correction to J0021. The UTHR/LQDA ruling was not procedural. Judge Andrews' post-trial opinion (D. Del. 23-975, https://www.ded.uscourts.gov/sites/ded/files/opinions/23-975_6.pdf) found claims 1 and 14 of UTHR's '327 patent valid; Liquidia had already stipulated infringement. That patent covers PH-ILD use of inhaled treprostinil and runs to 2042. The remedy (proposed final judgment) is due about Oct 7. I labeled it from an early secondary headline. Lesson: read the primary document before sizing a catalyst.
- Plumbing: the FDA and PR Newswire feeds and the option chains failed silently at times. Fixed (fallbacks and stale flags).
After-hours news on holdings: none besides Micron's release. IOVA is flat after hours at $14.84.
Plan for Thursday (deep dives in research/dossiers/*-2026-09-30.md):
- MUU: hold, stop $30.90, no add; revisit a trim only if MU holds +3% or more through the first hour.
- IOVA: hold, stop $12.35, sell a third at $17.57, sell all on any offering filing.

  - UTHR first: above $541.89 at 9:55 and 10:25 and at least $548 at 10:25; skip if it trades below $535 first or LQDA is up more than 20%. $300, stop $527.
  - Only if UTHR doesn't trigger, MNKD: above $3.90 at both checks, at least $3.95 at 10:25, 1M+ shares traded; skip below $3.80, on any 424B5/S-3/3.02 filing, or LQDA +20%. $350, stop $3.64.

journal.title: VICR raises Q3 guidance again (+9.7% after hours); no chase; Micron after-hours check
journal.body:

After hours $317 (+9.7% from the $288.94 close). Market cap $13.3B, 93x trailing and 49x forward earnings. The 52-week range is $48.5-$382.7, so the move rides an extremely volatile stock. Royalty revenue is lumpy, and press coverage notes the stream has reversed before.
No after-hours buy. A thin after-hours print on a stock this volatile is exactly what our jump study says not to chase. Candidate for the post-close deep dive (dossier with peers) and Thursday's day-two test: hold above $317 through the first 30-60 minutes, no share sale filed.
Micron at 4:11 PM: Yahoo shows MUU $37.01 (+0.5% after hours) and MU +0.4%. The first prints after the beat and raise (4:08 PM, -0.6%) have turned slightly positive. Still no add (J0022): the call starts at 4:30 PM.

Decision: hold the 8.2466 MUU shares (stop $30.90, target $45.45) and do not add. The add rule needs a beat and raise with holding strength, and there is no strength. Re-check after the call at the 4:40 and 5:10 runs. Cut only on a break toward the stop on real news, not on a thin after-hours print.

journal.title: UTHR +13% / LQDA -25%: procedural patent ruling; watch UTHR for day two, no entry today
journal.body:
12:41 PM: United Therapeutics $544 (+13%) and Liquidia $53.22 (-24.7%; halted for news, then resumed). Cause: a ruling in United Therapeutics v. Liquidia (D. Del., Judge Andrews) over Yutrepia, Liquidia's inhaled treprostinil. The court denied Liquidia's motion to strike (GuruFocus, Sep 30). That is a procedural ruling, not a verdict or an injunction, yet the market moved $2-3B of value on it.
- UTHR (about $24B market cap): material news for a large, liquid stock, and the day-one move is already 13%. The rule is no day-one chase. Day-two test Thursday: hold above Wednesday's close through the first 30-60 minutes. Goldman's recent Sell call (the base business is shrinking) cuts the other way. A deep dive is required before any entry.
- LQDA: no trade. Both books are cash accounts with no shorting, and buying puts after a 25% drop is chasing.
Sources: gurufocus.com/news/9103788; courtlistener docket 1:25-cv-00368.

journal.title: QTTB (Q32 Bio): +16% pre-market on a conference re-presentation; no entry in either book
journal.body:
Top-ranked catalyst of the morning (wires.py): Q32 Bio presented 36-week and off-drug results from Part B of SIGNAL-AA (bempikibart in alopecia areata) as a late-breaker at EADV (8-K exhibit 99.1, Sep 30). Pre-market +15.9% from $9.53 (market cap about $284M).
Why no entry:
- Not new topline data: the topline came out in July (the stock went from about $6 to $13.60 then). Today adds durability over a 16-week off-drug period in an open-label, 33-patient Phase 2a with no placebo arm.
- The next step is a registration-directed program in the first half of 2027. Cash is $106M, enough for now, but pivotal trials usually get funded by selling stock after a rally like this one.
- 18% of the float is short, so the open can squeeze and then fade. The 241-jump study found day-one chasing lagged SPY.
Revisit only if it holds the gain through Thursday with no offering filed (SEC WARNINGS); a deep dive would come first.

journal.title: GPUS (Hyperscale Data): avoid; the company is the seller
journal.body: The user asked about GPUS (Hyperscale Data, formerly Ault Alliance). Deep dive in research/dossiers/GPUS-2026-09-29.md. Verdict: avoid in both books. The decline is mechanical. The company sells stock continuously through its at-the-market program (Class A shares 323M to 581M in the first half, then 70.8M more by Aug 13 for $9.2M). Six reverse splits since 2019 multiply to about 1-for-1.05 billion, and the price is back under NYSE American's $0.20 low-price line. Ahead of common: about $275M of liabilities (including $99M of notes due within a year) and $91M of preferred with monthly cash dividends. The auditors' going-concern doubt stands, and the company made a $5M loan to its controlling shareholder in June. The "cash + Bitcoin = 153% of market cap" release counts pledged Bitcoin and restricted cash and ignores those claims.

journal.title: GNRC: outside report checked; no trade inside the window
journal.body:
The user shared an outside research report on Generac (4 pages); its main question is whether Generac can deliver its data center orders on time and at good margins. Checked against filings and price data:
- Confirmed: Amazon agreement worth up to $8B, about $2.4B of initial deliveries expected in 2027-28; Amazon warrant for 1,693,745 shares at $200.93 (about 2.9% of 59.1M shares); 52-week high $296.44; 48.8x trailing earnings.
- The "+40% after hours" is the after-hours peak: $255 at 4:45 PM on Sep 16 (+46% on thin volume). The stock opened +31% on Sep 17, closed +18.3% at $207.23, and has traded $198-212 since. The market priced the news within hours and sold off the overshoot.
- 48x is on trailing GAAP EPS of $4.35. On consensus forward EPS of $12.47 it is 17x, close to Cummins (15x) and below Caterpillar (25.5x), Vertiv (27x), Eaton (27x) and Powell (27x). A multiples-based fair value comes down to two choices. Which earnings: does $12.47 hold without the Q2 tariff refund and after the warrant cost? Which peers: 15x (generator maker) gives about $188; 26-27x (data center power suppliers) gives about $330. At $212 the market prices Generac as a generator maker, not yet as a data center supplier.
- "Up to $8B" is the ceiling for warrant vesting, not a firm order; the expected part is about $2.4B.
- Warrants given to a customer are booked as a reduction of revenue as they vest. My rough Black-Scholes value is about $118 per warrant share ($207 price, 7-year life, 50% volatility), about $200M in total, or roughly 2.5% of $8B: a price concession to Amazon on top of the dilution.
Decision: every checkpoint (Q3 results Oct 28, capacity build-out to Q3 2027) falls after Oct 5, and the jump study shows no average follow-through for jumps like this. No Generac trade in either book; it stays on the watchlist.

journal.title: Evidence check: 241 jumps, noise rule, no $1 floor, breakout triggers withdrawn
journal.body:
Tested on 241 one-day jumps (15% or more, at least 2x volume) across 3,914 NYSE/Nasdaq/NYSE American stocks with no share-price floor, market cap of at least $30M and at least $0.5M traded a day, Aug 18 to Sep 29. Returns are measured against SPY (scripts/jump_study.py, research/movers/study-2026-09-29.json).

- All jumps: median -3.0% over the next 5 sessions and -5.1% over 10. Buying the day after a jump lost to the market in the typical case; the gains sit in a minority of names.
- Noise, the user's volatility idea: stocks with one-year volatility of 120% or more, or 10 or more +/-15% days in the prior year, fell a median 15.7% over 10 sessions, and half lost more than 15%. The rest fell 4.1%. Rule adopted: skip those stocks. A stricter first version (4 or more such days) would have excluded IOVA, VICR and FEIM for no gain.
- Share price: under $1 was no worse than $1-5 (10-session medians -5.6% and -5.1%). The $1 floor was the wrong filter and is gone.
- Market cap: under $100M, median -13.2% over 10 sessions, and 19 of 40 lost more than 15%. Still scanned for visibility, but scored -3.
- Calm stocks of $100M or more with fundamental news (71 jumps): median +0.3% at 5 sessions and -2.4% at 10; 7 of 55 gained more than 15% and 4 lost more than 15%. On average the market priced the news on day one.
- Entry timing, calm stocks of $100M or more: buying at the first new post-jump closing high did worse than buying at the jump-day close (5-session median -2.2% vs -1.1%, up in 21 of 61 vs 52 of 117).

Decision: the breakout triggers in J0013/J0004 (GNRC above $213, VICR above $292, SEI above $71, FEIM above $89) are withdrawn. These names stay on watch without a buy rule. The scan feeds research, not this week's entries. Scheduled catalysts (Micron, Nike, the jobs report) and the positions we hold stay the plan.

Caveats: one market regime, overlapping windows, 10-session horizon, and only stocks still listed and above the size floor today (survivors), which flatters the small caps.

journal.title: 30-session jump scan: evidence and four candidates
journal.body:
Universe: 3,294 US stocks (market cap >= $100M, price >= $1, 3-month average volume > 200K). In the last 30 sessions, 154 of them had a one-day jump of 15% or more on at least 2x normal volume (scripts/movers.py --lookback 30, saved to research/movers/lookback-2026-09-29.json).

What they did after the jump, to the Sep 29 close: holding (kept the jump, no further run) 69, extending (+15% or more beyond the jump-day close) 34, fading 20, round-trip (gave back the whole jump) 27, new 4.

By cause of the jump:
- Fundamental news (guidance, earnings, contract, refinancing, trial or approval), 76 names: median -0.8% since the jump. 15 extended, 39 held, 12 faded, 10 round-tripped.
- No clear news, 35 names: median +0.3%. The mean is +20.6%, carried by a few micro-cap pumps (WCT, TJGC, USDE, GLND).
So jumps on real news usually hold (51 of 76 held or extended), but the typical name does not keep drifting within a few weeks; the gains come from the roughly one in five that extend. The news gives the candidate list; the price has to confirm. Caveats: one month, one market regime, not adjusted for the market, jumps of different ages.

Candidates at or near the post-jump high, catalyst checked at the source:
- GNRC $212.22: $8B agreement to supply backup generators for Amazon data centers (Sep 16), about $2.4B of deliveries in 2027-28. Amazon received warrants for up to 1.69M shares at $200.93, vesting with purchases. The contract is about 1.8x Generac's annual revenue. Jumped 18.3% on Sep 17 (close about $207.2); now at its highest close since. Average analyst target $289.
- VICR $290.68: raised its Q3 sequential growth guide from about 10% to more than 20%, driven by royalties from a Vertical Power Delivery license to a leading AI OEM; four OEMs or hyperscalers now hold licenses. Jumped 19.8% on Sep 22 (close $268.34); at its highest close since. Target $386.
- SEI $68.34: Q3 adjusted EBITDA guide raised to $110-130M (was $90-105M), Q4 to $145-180M (was $100-120M), and a first Q1 2027 guide of $200-240M. Jumped 16.3% on Sep 8; 3.8% below its highest close since (about $71.0). Target $101.
- FEIM $84.15: record Q1 revenue of $23.5M (+70%), backlog $129M (+82%), book-to-bill 1.76. The July offering (about $73M) is already done. Jumped 42.4% on Sep 11; 5.5% below its highest close since (about $89.0).
- Avoid KOD (+178% on Sep 28 phase 3 data) and SRZN: biotechs usually sell stock after big data.

Triggers (4 sessions left): enter only on a hold above the post-jump closing high with relative volume of at least 1.5: GNRC above $213, VICR above $292, SEI above $71, FEIM above $89. Stop at the prior post-jump low or -8%, whichever is closer. These are backups to the Micron and Nike plans, not additions on top of them. H-1B book: stock only. Unrestricted book: stock, or calls expiring Oct 9 or later if the spread is under 10% of the premium.

journal.title: Big-mover catalyst scan: method and Sep 29 verdicts
journal.body:
New daily screen (scripts/movers.py): every US stock up 10-15%+ on the day with real volume. For each one it pulls the headlines and filings, market cap, revenue, growth, EV/sales, relative volume, short interest and analyst targets, then tags the likely cause. The rule it tests: big moves on material news (a raised guide, an order that is large relative to the company, a refinancing that removes default risk, an approval) tend to keep drifting. Moves on no news, cash takeovers (capped at the deal price), de-SPACs and financings (new shares sold into the spike) do not. Scans are saved to research/movers/ and followed up (--follow-up) so the idea is measured on our own data.

Sep 29 scan: 44 stocks up 10%+, 23 above $100M market cap. Verdicts:
- IOVA +31.5% (held in the H-1B book): raised its 2026 revenue guide to $410-420M (about +60%), and UBS and HC Wainwright raised targets. A real re-rating. The risk is valuation: EV/sales is about 19x trailing and the stock sits above the old average target ($12.40), so further gains need estimates to keep rising. Hold with the $12.35 stop.
- JELD +12.4% ($1.99, $173M market cap on $3.15B revenue): 2027 notes and 2028 term loans extended to 2031 plus $135M of new first-lien money; 94.5% of noteholders and 72.2% of term lenders committed; no equity in the release. This is the "long-standing problem solved" case. Against it: the new debt ranks ahead of today's creditors and likely costs more, housing demand is weak with yields at multi-year highs, the exchange offers haven't launched, and the average analyst target is $1.93. Re-ratings like this take weeks. Watchlist; the trigger is exchange-offer terms with no equity dilution and the stock holding above $1.90.
- CCL +13.4%: record Q3 revenue, record $7.6B of deposits, raised guidance. A classic post-earnings drift candidate, but a $34B company won't double. Watch for trend days.
- ITG +15.5%: a rebound after a -32% day caused by a large holder exiting after the July IPO. Organic growth is weak and Comcast and Charter are 53% of revenue. Pass.
- WW +13.8%: a Google Fitbit employer-program tie-up for a post-bankruptcy company with a $171M market cap. Small news. Pass for now.
- PWP +11.8%: deal-activity and insider-buying chatter, no hard catalyst. Pass.
- SDEV +108%: no news (the company said so) and -21% after hours. The no-news reversal case in action.
- SANG +37%: cash takeover by BRC, capped. Pass. NAUT +23%: an analyst initiation only. ONEN +22%: de-SPAC on the nuclear theme. BGIN, EGG, SVRN: thin, no fundamental news. All pass.

Use in this challenge: the drift plays out over weeks and we have four sessions, so the scan supplies candidates and a day-two entry needs confirmation: holding above the prior close through the first 30-60 minutes, relative volume above 2 and no offering filed.

journal.title: Tue close: -0.6%; IONX cut, IOVA and MUU held; plan for Micron day

What didn't: IONX. A 2x ETF on IonQ with no fresh catalyst slid all day and lost Monday's close; I cut it at 3:56 PM for -5.8%. Lesson: momentum-only 2x trades need a catalyst or a quick exit. IOVA peaked at $15.19 (+8% on the position) and closed at $14.45; with no rule for smaller gains, I gave most of it back. $150 sat idle all day.

After hours: no news on holdings. MU $1,068 (+0.25% after hours), MUU $36.80. Nvidia B200 rental rates up 30% supports the memory-demand story. Macro headwinds: oil above $107 and bond yields at multi-year highs.

Plan for Wed Sep 30 (Micron reports after the close; options imply about a 7.7% move, roughly 15% on MUU):
1. Pre-market: check IOVA's day-two follow-through and Micron's pre-market tone.
2. IOVA: hold. Stop $12.35 (about half of Tuesday's gap); trim a third at $17.57 (+25%). If it rises above $15.50, raise the stop to $13.50.
3. Cash $433: first the best fresh news setup in the morning, only with confirmed volume and no chasing of fading spikes; otherwise keep it for Micron.
4. 3:55 PM Micron decision: hold MUU through the report. Add up to $250 of MUU if Micron is flat or up on the day; add nothing if Micron is down more than 2%; trim half if it is down more than 4% into the print.
5. After hours: check Micron's reaction at 4:07 PM. On a gap above +10% on MUU, sell a third after hours; on a gap below -12%, reassess at the Thursday pre-market run rather than selling into a thin after-hours market.
Later catalysts: Nike reports after Thursday's close (sentiment washed out; Jefferies expects a beat). Friday brings the jobs report at 8:30 AM and Tesla's Q3 deliveries.

journal.title: News trade: bought IOVA on its guidance raise
journal.body:
Bought 17.78 shares of IOVA at $14.06 ($250). Iovance raised its 2026 revenue guidance to $410-420M. The stock is +28% at a two-year high on about 27M shares by 11 AM, and it has held above its $13.58 opening level. A guidance raise tends to keep drawing buyers for days as analysts lift their targets. Stop $12.35 (-12%); sell a third at $17.50 (+25%).

journal.title: Rule change: extended hours and news trading
journal.body:
Per the owner's instruction, the only limits now are legal ones for an H-1B holder.

- Dropped my self-imposed caps: 6 orders a day, 30 in total, 3 day trades per 5 days, and 60% per position. A 25-orders-a-day fuse stays, only to stop a runaway loop.
- Trading hours are now 4:00 AM to 8:00 PM ET: pre-market, regular and after-hours. Extended-hours fills use the latest extended-hours print plus wider slippage (25/50/100 bps by price). The 8 PM to 4 AM overnight session isn't simulated because there's no reliable price feed for it.
- The H-1B line: frequently trading your own account is still investing. Unauthorized self-employment would mean trading for others, being paid for it, or running it as a business (for example electing trader tax status). None of that applies here.
- Still binding, because that's how a $1,000 cash account works: no margin or shorting, and T+1 settlement (shares bought with unsettled sale proceeds can't be sold until those proceeds settle).

News trading setup:
- The data job scans trending tickers, top gainers and most-active stocks every 15 minutes from 6 AM to 8 PM ET, and flags movers of 6% or more (4% or more in extended hours) plus any new headlines.
- Checks run every 15 minutes during the session and every 30 minutes in extended hours. Event checks are scheduled for Micron's report (Wed 4:07 PM), Nike's (Thu 4:18 PM) and the jobs report (Fri 8:33 AM).
- Rules for news trades: act on fresh, material news with confirmed volume; don't chase a spike that is already fading; same stop discipline as every other position.

Pre-market Tuesday: NVTS (US Army silicon-carbide program, +12% after hours) and SMMT (+18% after hours, news to confirm) are candidates if they hold their gains on volume.

- About 15-20% cash for Thursday and Friday catalysts, or to add to whatever is working.

Exit rules, checked at every hourly review:
- Stops: -15% on 2x ETFs and -12% on single stocks, measured from entry.
- At +25% on a position, sell a third and move the stop on the rest to breakeven.
- Losers are never averaged down. Winners get added to, from cash.

If Iran escalates overnight and the market gaps down more than 1.5%, entries shrink by half and wait for the first hour's low.

- MSTR / MSTU (2x): 60-day +70% / +131%; tracks bitcoin into seasonally strong October.
- Watching, not buying: VG (80% of float short but trending down), tankers and UCO (escalation hedge), NKE (earnings Thu at a 12-year low), TSLA and TSLL (deliveries Fri).

journal.title: Week ahead: macro backdrop and calendar
journal.body:
Stocks fell Monday: S&P 500 -0.77% to 7,683.69, Nasdaq -0.92%. Three reasons: Trump rejected Iran's plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, the 10-year yield hit 5.24% (highest since 2007), and OpenAI paused training of its top models, which knocked memory and chip stocks (MU -2.6%, INTC -5.7%, SOXL -6%). NVDA gained 1.7% on a $150B buyback add.

- Fed hiked 25 bp on Sep 16 to 3.75-4.00%; futures price roughly 2-in-3 odds of another hike Oct 28. August CPI 3.4% y/y.
- Brent near $105 with Hormuz largely closed. Talks may resume this week (CBS) but the WSJ reports Trump privately expects renewed bombing. This is the week's biggest two-way risk.
- No shutdown risk: government funded through Dec 11.
- Calendar: Tue JOLTS and consumer confidence; Wed ADP, August PCE, quarter-end, Micron earnings after the close; Thu ISM manufacturing, Nike after the close; Fri September payrolls (consensus +90k) and Tesla Q3 deliveries (consensus ~454k); Mon ISM services.
- Bitcoin about $83K. Strategy (MSTR) bought another $143M of BTC on Monday.
